meta.title: Aakash Chowdhury
meta.description: Under the supervision of Elisabeth Oswald, I recently completed my doctoral thesis on statistical and machine-learning methods for side-channel security evaluation. I am currently working on an interdisciplinary project on the notion of "explainability" in side-channel security evaluation. Before my PhD, I completed my Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Statistics from Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, respectively.

hero.kicker: SECURITY RESEARCHER · MACHINE LEARNING & AI ENTHUSIAST
hero.headline:
Making sense of
leakage.
hero.intro: Under Elisabeth Oswald, I recently completed my doctoral thesis titled "Towards the Advancement of Side-Channel Security Evaluation through Statistical and Machine Learning Methods" at the University of Klagenfurt, Austria, and I plan to defend it by January 2027. Currently, I am working on an interdisciplinary project exploring "explainability" in side-channel leakage assessment. I hold Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Statistics from Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, so anything related to applied machine learning methods in security research interests me.

recentActivities.title: Exploring security research
recentActivities.description: My recent work focuses on statistical and machine-learning methods for profiled and non-profiled side-channel security evaluation, including leakage detection, leakage certification, efficient leakage exploitation, and explainable security assessment.

card.title: Explainable AI for leakage assessment
card.description: Developing interpretable, data-driven methods to understand how leakage signals emerge and how they should be assessed in practice.

card.title: Efficient leakage exploitation
card.description: Studying practical attacks that recover sensitive information with fewer traces and improved statistical efficiency.

card.title: Multivariate leakage detection
card.description: Applied multivariate and univariate statistical tests to detect hidden leakage in embedded cryptographic implementations.

card.title: Leakage certification
card.description: Studied mutual-information-based certification methods and rigorous statistical evidence for security claims.

item.title: Multivariate Leakage Detection
item.description: Aakash Chowdhury & Elisabeth Oswald. A study of non-specific multivariate leakage detection methods, including distance covariance and classical multivariate approaches, with simulated and practical side-channel case studies.

item.title: Leakage Certification Made Simple
item.description: Aakash Chowdhury, Carlo Brunetta, Arnab Roy & Elisabeth Oswald. Mutual-information-based approaches and implementations for side-channel leakage certification.
